answer: The only solutions are f(x) = x + c for any constant c ≥ 0.
claims: g(x) = f(x) - x satisfies g(x + g(x)) = g(x) and g(x) ≥ 0 for all x > 0
The squared differences yield the exact bound |g(x)-g(y)|(2x+2y+g(x)+g(y)) ≤ (x-y-g(y))²
All positive values of g are equal to a single constant c ≥ 0
The range of g cannot be {0, c} with c > 0 (connectedness of (0,∞))
Therefore g is constant, so f(x) = x + c with c ≥ 0
assumptions: Connectedness of (0, ∞) in the standard topology

mechanisms.name: functional-equation-from-equality-case
mechanisms.summary: Setting x = f(y) forces equality in both outer inequalities, yielding f(f(y)) = 2f(y) - y.

mechanisms.name: iterate-linearization
mechanisms.summary: From g(x+g(x)) = g(x) we get fⁿ(x) = x + n g(x), which forces g(x) ≥ 0 by positivity.

mechanisms.name: exact-squared-difference-decomposition
mechanisms.summary: Squaring both inequalities and subtracting gives R = ¼[(x-y-B)² + (A-B)(2x+2y+A+B)] and L = ¼[(x-y-B)² - (A-B)(2x+2y+A+B)], combining to the tight bound (1).

mechanisms.name: orbit-growth-argument
mechanisms.summary: On forward orbits g takes constant values A,B; choosing m to keep RHS bounded while LHS grows linearly forces A = B.

mechanisms.name: topological-separation
mechanisms.summary: If g takes both 0 and c > 0, the separation inequality makes both level sets open, contradicting connectedness of (0,∞).

falsification_attempts.attack: Iterates fⁿ(x) = x + n g(x) must remain positive for all n ∈ ℕ
falsification_attempts.outcome: Falsified: g(x) < 0 would make fⁿ(x) negative for large n

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: g could take two distinct positive values A ≠ B
falsification_attempts.attack: Use orbits x+nA, y+mB with m chosen to make |x+nA-y-mB-B| ≤ B/2; RHS of (1) bounded by B²/4 while LHS ~ 2nA|A-B| → ∞
falsification_attempts.outcome: Falsified: forces all positive values equal

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: g could take values {0, c} with c > 0
falsification_attempts.attack: For x with g(x)=c and y with g(y)=0, inequality (2) gives |x-y| ≥ √(c(2x+c)) and |x-y| ≥ √(c(2y+c)), making both level sets open
falsification_attempts.outcome: Falsified: (0,∞) cannot be partitioned into two disjoint nonempty open sets

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: f(x) = kx might work for k ≠ 1
falsification_attempts.attack: Direct substitution into left inequality yields quadratic form condition requiring k=1
falsification_attempts.outcome: Falsified: only k=1 works, which is the c=0 case

evidence: Algebraic derivation of bound (1) is internally verifiable
Inductive proof of fⁿ(x) = x + n g(x) from g(x+g(x)) = g(x)
Orbit argument uses only elementary Diophantine approximation (nearest integer)
Topological argument uses standard connectedness of (0,∞)
Verification step uses only QM-AM-GM inequality
